items.title: The Scout listens to Inez

beats.speaker: milena
beats.line: Inez, have you eaten anything since the morning? You've hardly left that doorway all shift.

beats.speaker: waitress
beats.line: I'll eat when I've caught up. The Bureau sent another notice this week, and I'm two payments behind already.

beats.speaker: milena
beats.line: Only two? I'm three behind, and we'll both still be paying them off when we're old and grey.

beats.speaker: waitress
beats.line: Don't, Milena. Some days I'd give anything just to sit down for a little while.

beats.speaker: milena
beats.line: You wouldn't sit for long. You'd be up again the moment the guard on the Office door looked this way.

beats.speaker: waitress
beats.line: What do you mean by that?

beats.speaker: milena
beats.line: Only that you've looked across that square more often today than you've looked at your own tables.

beats.speaker: waitress
beats.line: Has Arthur said something to you?

beats.speaker: milena
beats.line: He's never said a word to me. You've just told me his name yourself, love.
beats.revealAfter: He's never said a word to me.

beats.speaker: waitress
beats.line: Oh, Milena. Yes, it's Arthur, and nobody knows, and nobody can know.

beats.speaker: milena
beats.line: Why ever not? He seems a decent enough man, from what I can see of him from here.

beats.speaker: waitress
beats.line: Because if the Office hears of it, he'll lose his post, and I'll lose him. I can't afford to lose anything else.

beats.speaker: milena
beats.line: Then it won't come from me. But stop looking across at him, or someone else will see what I saw.

beats.speaker: waitress
beats.line: I know. I'll keep my eyes on my tables, I promise.

beats.speaker: scout
beats.line: She owes the Bureau more than she can pay, and she's seeing Arthur on the Office door. She'd want neither known.

notes: Same facts, same order of discovery: the Bureau and being behind; the guard; she gives his name away herself; if the Office hears, it costs them both.
One question at a time: Inez's "Who says? Did Arthur say something? Who else has he told?" becomes "What do you mean by that?", then, after Milena answers, "Has Arthur said something to you?".
Milena's reveal keeps its beat ("He's never said a word to me." first, the rest 0.9 s later).
The Scout's last line says only what was heard. Today's "We could clear her Bureau loan, or use Arthur on the door." is gone: the cards after the cut (Help, Pressure) already say what's open.

items.title: The Fixer pays Inez's loan, first visit

beats.speaker: fixer
beats.line: Forgive me for stopping you between tables, Miss Nikolaou. I've just paid part of your loan at the Bureau.

beats.speaker: waitress
beats.line: You've done what?

beats.speaker: fixer
beats.line: Paid part of it. It's stamped and filed, so it'll be on your card at the Bureau by the end of the day.

beats.speaker: waitress
beats.line: I don't know you. How do you know what I owe?

beats.speaker: fixer
beats.line: People talk in a square like this one. I listen, and I don't repeat what I hear.

beats.speaker: waitress
beats.line: Did anyone see you go in there for me?

beats.speaker: fixer
beats.line: Nobody who'd care. It's a payment at a counter, and they take a hundred of those a day.

beats.speaker: waitress
beats.line: Nobody pays a stranger's debts for nothing. What is it you want from me?

beats.speaker: fixer
beats.line: Nothing today. One day soon I may ask you a small favour, and it won't hurt anybody.

beats.speaker: waitress
beats.line: Then I'm grateful, truly. But I can't promise you anything for it, not yet.

beats.speaker: fixer
beats.line: I haven't asked you to. Take today as it comes, and I'll come back with the rest.

beats.speaker: waitress
beats.line: You'd pay all of it? Nobody does that for a stranger.

beats.speaker: fixer
beats.line: Then I'll be the first. Go back to your tables, Miss Nikolaou, before anyone wonders who I am.

notes: "Who are you? Who told you about that? Who saw you come?" becomes three questions in three turns, each answered before the next: How do you know? Did anyone see? What do you want?
Still says, in these words, that he'll come back with the rest; she took it and isn't ready.
The last line keeps the steel under the warmth without a threat.

items.title: The Fixer pays Inez's loan, second visit

beats.speaker: fixer
beats.line: That's the rest of it paid, Miss Nikolaou. You don't owe the Bureau a single thing.

beats.speaker: waitress
beats.line: Please, not so loud. People can hear you from the terrace.

beats.speaker: fixer
beats.line: Forgive me. I forget how far a voice carries out here.

beats.speaker: waitress
beats.line: I've owed them for years. I keep waiting to feel lighter, and I don't, not yet.

beats.speaker: fixer
beats.line: Give it a day or two. You kept up longer than most people would have managed.

beats.speaker: waitress
beats.line: You said you'd bring the rest, and you did. So what is it you want from me?

beats.speaker: fixer
beats.line: A few minutes of someone's time. When I telephone the café, I'd like you to call Arthur over from his door.

beats.speaker: waitress
beats.line: So you know about us. How long have you known?

beats.speaker: fixer
beats.line: Long enough to know it's nobody's business but yours. Nobody will hear it from me.

beats.speaker: waitress
beats.line: What happens to him, if I call him over?

beats.speaker: fixer
beats.line: Nothing, if this goes the way it should. He'll be at your side, and he'll never see us.

beats.speaker: waitress
beats.line: He won't leave that door for nothing. I'll tell him I've something to say that can't go down a telephone.

beats.speaker: fixer
beats.line: Then tell him that. You know him better than anyone does.

beats.speaker: waitress
beats.line: You kept your word to me, so I'll keep mine.

beats.speaker: waitress
beats.line: I watch that square all day anyway. If I see trouble coming before you telephone, I'll find a way to warn you.

notes: Sky agreed today's version on 2026-11-01; this reopens it. The ask, the fright at "Arthur", what happens to him, her reason for the guard and her offer to warn are all kept.
"Thank you, I mean that. Your turn. What do I owe?" (three thoughts) becomes a line of relief that doesn't come yet, then one question.
Her reason for getting him off the door (something that can't go down a telephone) is now hers, said aloud, which the call scene already relies on.

items.title: The Fixer pays Lukac

beats.speaker: driver
beats.line: So it's paid. It's been a lean month, and I won't pretend I'm not glad of it.

beats.speaker: fixer
beats.line: I'm glad it helps. All we want is one short drive with the Councillor, and an easy one.

beats.speaker: driver
beats.line: I've been promised easy drives before. Tell me exactly where it goes.

beats.speaker: fixer
beats.line: When the chime goes, he'll come out and get in as he always does. But you don't take him home this time.

beats.speaker: driver
beats.line: Then where do I take him?

beats.speaker: fixer
beats.line: Round to the service bay at the back of the Office. You pull in there and wait.

beats.speaker: driver
beats.line: The east yard, round the back. And how long am I meant to sit there with him?

beats.speaker: fixer
beats.line: Not long. Just until we've got him.

beats.speaker: driver
beats.line: I've heard 'not long' before. I'll give you a couple of minutes, and then I drive on.

beats.speaker: fixer
beats.line: That's fair, Lukac. A couple of minutes, and we'll be waiting at the bay when you pull in.

beats.speaker: driver
beats.line: And don't tell me who 'we' are. What I don't know, nobody can ask me about later.

beats.speaker: fixer
beats.line: I wish everyone I dealt with had your sense, Lukac.

beats.speaker: driver
beats.line: Sense doesn't pay the rent. If anyone's hanging about watching that bay, though, I can send them off.

beats.speaker: fixer
beats.line: Do that, and we'll take it from there.

beats.speaker: driver
beats.line: Whatever happens at that bay, I won't be looking.

notes: Sky agreed today's version on 2026-11-02; this reopens it. Same job: at the chime, the service bay (east yard), a couple of minutes, then Lukac drives on; can send off anyone watching the bay; doesn't want to know who "we" are, and now says why.
"It's paid, then. It's been a lean month. For what, exactly?" becomes a line of relief and a question in its own turn.
The Fixer likes Lukac once, out loud.
